observations:
Torah #89 has zero bechina edges in the dataset and only one bechina equivalence in the source text (שכינה / אלקים — two nodes). The threshold for proposing a new package is 3 or more concepts forming an independent bechina domain. The single gap pair identified (שכינה = אלקים) is two nodes — below the threshold.

The full concept inventory of Torah #89 from the source text is small:
  (1) חסרון (human deficiency) — appears as the subject of the teaching
  (2) שכינה — the locus of the deficiency; identified via bechina as אלקים
  (3) אלקים — the divine name = the Shekhinah (the explicit bechina pair)
  (4) צער ועצבות (sorrow and sadness) — the negative emotional state that would result from knowing about the deficiency (mentioned only to be overcome)
  (5) כבוד וגדולה (honor and greatness) — the reframing: that the King shares His deficiency is itself a great honor
  (6) שמחה גדולה (great joy) — the emotion that results from the reframing
  (7) מחין חדשים (new/renewed intellect) — the spiritual outcome of the joy
  (8) המלך (the King / God) — the one who shares the deficiency

Of these, only items (2) and (3) are in a bechina relationship with each other. Items (4)-(7) are stages of an eitza chain. Items (1) and (8) are narrative anchors. No grouping of 3+ concepts forms an independent bechina domain that would warrant a new package.

Conclusion: NO_NEW_PACKAGES. The correct action for this Torah is to add the bechina edge שכינה / אלקים to the dataset (see torah_89_additions.json), which would create the first package for Torah #89 — a good, two-node package — but it does not qualify as a 'new package proposal' since it falls below the 3-node threshold and is a gap-fill rather than a novel domain discovery.
